slides.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE CASTLES IN THE AIR To have big dreams about an idea or project that may not come true. What if all this had been just castles in the air? CLASS ACT A person or thing displaying impressive and stylish excellence. The writing and the look of the magazine make it a real class act. HUNKY DORY Expression used to say all is going well. Everything is hunky-dory. QUEER AS A THREE-DOLLAR BILL Completely and obviously false or fake; not genuine or authentic in the slightest.. The guy claims to teach you how to get rich in a hurry, but the whole thing sounds as queer as a three-dollar bill. LARGER THAN LIFE To attract special attention because of unusual and flamboyant appearance or behavior or seem disproportionately important. Your problems seem larger than life at that time of the night. OFF THE MARK When something or someone is incorrect or inaccurate. The accusation was a little wide of the mark. OFF BASE To be mistaken. Your argument is so off base. OFF THE WALL To be eccentric or unconventional. Some other times to be really angry. The president was off the wall about the article.

Language bricks

slides.title: We are able to express ideas about things or event that did not happen through the use of different expressions and regular grammar.
visibleTexts: We are able to express ideas about things or event that did not happen through the use of different expressions and regular grammar.

PHRASES EXAMPLES What if… What if Charles had taken Mary to the party? He would have loosened there! Imagine that / if… Imagine you hadn’t called Joe’s parents; When would have they known? Suppose / Supposing that Supposing we had not gone to the doctor, we could have gotten worse. I wish… I wish I had called her; now, I will never know if she felt the same for me. To Consider 1. We work with these phrases using the past perfect tense. 2. When using what if we have to close the sentence with a question mark. 3. Could and would play a major role. Especially for complementing the sentences. 4. Some other modals may be useful depending on the context.

Functions Examples Express ideas or events that did not happen. What if Jill had gotten his new car? Now, he lost the chance. Imagine Julius and Meg had gotten married, they would not have lasted two months. Suppose that we had not arrived on time, he could have lost his flight. I wish he hadn’t said that to the principal.
To consider When we use wish with past perfect, we talked about wishes in the past; something that never came to be true.

C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read the text aloud to your teacher. Check the full article in the link below.

Global Disasters that never Came to happen: The Impending Ice Age An April 28, 1975 article in Newsweek Magazine titled "The Cooling World" warned that the world could freeze over before we knew it. A year earlier, Time ran an article titled, "A New Ice Age?" The media of the mid-70's latched onto the idea of impending icy death, imagine if it had become true. But where did this come from? Between 1945 and the 1970's global temperatures had decreased. Scientists have since figured out that sulphate aerosols caused cooling, by blocking and reflecting sunlight as well as serving as seeds for cloud coverage. At the same time scientific papers explaining about how the earth's orbital patterns affect global weather and the creation of ice ages were being published. The media seemed to pick up geologist saying an ice age could be soon — but not really understanding that thousands of years is "soon" to a geologist; but what if that had happened? We would not probable have written this article. Despite the media hype, the scientific journals were either unsure about how humans were affecting the climate, or already predicting the possibility of global warming due to CO2. Current research shows the high level of CO2 in the atmosphere is preventing any growth of the ice sheets. The Ice Age fear has come back recently, most likely because of the 2012 hysteria, but this time in conjunction with the sun's solar cycles. Bad Astronomy explains why you don't need invest in parkas quite yet. Incidentally, Newsweek issued a correction to the 1975 article in 2006, since by then it was clear an Ice Age hadn't wiped us all out. If only people had been more cautious in the information they linked, we (new generations) may have turned more eager for facts than farandula.
